So x11(x) and x12(x) should be functions.

x11 = chain(x10, halve, size) = lambda x: x10(halve(size(x))). size(x) is integer (number of cells in object). halve gives n//2. x10 = lbind(lbind, greater) = lbind applied... x10(y) = lbind(greater, y) = lambda z: greater(y, z)? Wait lbind(function, fixed) fixes leftmost arg: lbind(greater, y) = lambda z: greater(y, z) = y > z. So x11(obj) = a function that tests greater(n//2, z) where n = size of object.

x12 = compose(x9, x6) = lambda x: x9(x6(x)). x6 = compose(x5, toindices) = lambda obj: x5(toindices(obj)). toindices converts object to frozenset of indices. x5 = rbind(extract, x4) = lambda container: extract(container, x4) where x4 = compose(x3, initset) = lambda cell: x3(initset(cell)). x3 = lbind(adjacent, x2) = lambda patch: adjacent(patch, x2). x2 = outbox(x1) where x1 = asindices(I) = all grid indices. outbox of full grid: uppermost-1 = -1, lowermost+1 = h, leftmost-1=-1, rightmost+1=w. So the outbox is the border around the grid (outside). Actually outbox computes lines at rows si..ei and cols sj..ej, si=-1, ei=h, sj=-1, ej=w. So it's the frame one cell outside the grid.

So x2 is the frame outside the grid. x3(patch) = adjacent(patch, x2) = manhattan distance between patch and frame == 1. That's true iff patch touches the border of the grid (a cell adjacent to outside). x5 = extract first element satisfying x4... Hmm x5(container) = extract(container, x4) where x4(cell) = x3(initset(cell)) = adjacent({cell}, x2). So it extracts the first cell in the container that is on the grid border.

For a vertical bar of height >= 2 starting at bottom and ending at top... Actually bars rise from bottom. The bottom cell is always adjacent to the frame (bottom border). So extract returns the bottom cell of the bar (first found by iteration order of frozenset — nondeterministic-ish but it's the bottom cell since it's the only border cell? Unless the bar reaches the top row too, then top cell also border. But generally bars rise from bottom and don't reach top).

So x6(obj) = bottom cell index of the bar.

x9 = chain(x7, x8, initset): x7 = rbind(compose, initset) = lambda f: compose(f, initset)? Wait rbind(manhattan, fixed) = lambda x: manhattan(x, fixed). lbind(rbind, manhattan) fixes leftmost arg of rbind: = lambda y: rbind(manhattan, y) = lambda y: lambda patch: manhattan(patch, y). So x8(initset(cell)) = rbind(manhattan, {cell}) = lambda patch: manhattan(patch, {cell}).

Then x7(that) = compose(that, initset) = lambda x: that(initset(x)) = lambda x: manhattan({x}, {cell}) hmm wait careful. Let me just think of the final meaning.

x12 = x9(x6(obj)) = x9(bottomcell). x9(x) as computed: x7(x8(initset(x))) where initset(x)={x}. x8({x}) = lambda patch: manhattan(patch, {x}). x7 = lambda f: lambda z: f(initset(z)) = lambda z: f({z}). Then x13 = fork(compose, x11, x12) = lambda x: compose(x11(x), x12(x)) = lambda z: x11(x)(x12(x)(z)) = (n//2) > dist(z, bottom).

So x13(obj) is a function on cell z: true if dist(z, bottom) < n//2 where n = size (height) of bar, i.e. distance from bottom is 0,1,..., n//2 - 1.

Then x14 = fork(sfilter, toindices, x13) = lambda obj: sfilter(toindices(obj), x13(obj)). So it keeps cells whose distance from bottom is less than n//2.

x15 = mapply(x14, x0) = union over objects of those cells.

x16 = fill(I, 8, x15).
